resolutions.finding: C1 TIMEOUT: R036 says 'default timeout 120 s, 300 s for push, fetch, pull, worktree add, the forge CLIs, `add -A` and diff'; critic says commitAll's `add -A` has no timeout.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Git.swift:31-36 declares `func run(_ arguments: [String], environment extra: [String: String] = [:], input: Data? = nil, timeout: TimeInterval = 120)`. Git.swift:163-166 `commitAll(message:)` is exactly: `try Self.check(await run(["add", "-A"]))` then `try Self.check(await run(["commit", "-F", "-"], input: Data(message.utf8)))`. NEITHER call passes `timeout:`, so both run at the 120 s default. Counted by grep: `timeout: 300` occurs exactly 18 times in Git.swift, at lines 169, 181, 186, 191, 216, 217, 218, 253, 286, 290, 404, 448, 459, 484, 558, 566, 679, 707. Of those, 6 (181, 186, 191, 216, 217, 218) are `Shell.run(tool:)` forge-CLI calls, not git. The 12 git calls at 300 s are: push HEAD (169), captureTree(paths:) scratch add (253), pushBranch (286), fetch (290), pullFastForward (404), incremental scratch add (448), scratch full add (459), throwaway-index full add (484), diff single-chunk (558), diff per-chunk (566), addDetachedWorktree (679), apply's throwaway-index add (707). There is no other `timeout:` literal in Git.swift (only the declaration at :35 and the pass-through at :47). So the 300 s `add -A` invocations are ALL index-file-redirected (GIT_INDEX_FILE) snapshot adds; the only `add -A` against the user's real index, commitAll's, gets 120 s. `diff` IS at 300 s on both branches, so R036 was right about diff and wrong about `add -A`.
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows port must give `git add -A` and `git commit -F -` in the commit-all path a 120 s budget, and 300 s only to the 12 enumerated git calls plus the 6 forge-CLI calls. On Windows, where `add -A` over a large tree is materially slower than on APFS, this 120 s ceiling is the one most likely to fire; copy it anyway, and reproduce the failure as `ShellError(result.failureMessage)` from the terminate-then-SIGKILL path (Shell.swift:110-118; the port's equivalent is TerminateProcess after a 1 s grace).

resolutions.finding: C2 UNREACHABLE STRING: R036 lists 'The request could not be merged.' as error text surfaced to the user.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Git.swift:210-227 `mergePullRequest(_ link: MergeRequestLink)`. Line 212: `var lastFailure = "The request could not be merged."`. Line 213: `for attempt in 0..<6 {`. A Swift half-open range 0..<6 is non-empty, so the body always executes at least once. Inside: line 220 `if result.succeeded { return }`; line 221 `lastFailure = result.failureMessage`. Every path out of an iteration either returns or has already assigned lastFailure. Line 226 `throw ShellError(lastFailure)` is only reachable after at least one assignment. Shell.swift:15-19 `failureMessage` = trimmed stderr, else trimmed stdout, else `"The command failed with exit code \(status)."` -- never empty. Repo-wide grep for `could not be merged` returns exactly one hit: Git.swift:212. The literal is therefore dead: it can never reach a user. R036 did not classify it.
resolutions.port_impact: The port keeps the initializer literal for byte-for-byte source parity if it wants, but must NOT put it in any localization table, test expectation, or user-visible string inventory. The user-visible text for a failed merge is always the forge CLI's own stderr, or `"The command failed with exit code <n>."`. Note the separate, genuinely reachable literal at Shell.swift:129-131 (see CC4).

resolutions.finding: C3 SCRATCH-INDEX FALLBACK: R036 says currentTree's capture closure, when scratch is nil or the incremental add fails, deletes the scratch, re-seeds and runs `add -A -- .`
resolutions.port_impact: Two distinct fallbacks, both must exist. (a) No stream / cookie never arrived -> a private, UUID-named, delete-on-exit index, seeded from the real index or HEAD. (b) Stream present but the incremental add failed -> delete and rebuild the SHARED scratch. Collapsing them would either share an index across a torn-down watch or leak a per-call index. On Windows, the copy-the-real-index seeding (CopyFile of .git/index) preserves git's stat cache exactly as on macOS; keep it, because it is what makes the unchanged-file fast path work.

resolutions.finding: G1 checkpointRef: the two shipped `phase` literals, the persisted fields holding the resulting refs, and their migration behaviour.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Git.swift:409-411:
```
static func checkpointRef(thread: UUID, turn: Int, phase: String) -> String {
    "refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/\(thread.uuidString.lowercased())/\(turn)-\(phase)"
}
```
Repo-wide grep for `checkpointRef` gives exactly two call sites, hence exactly TWO phase literals, both verbatim lowercase:
- ThreadRuntime.swift:1226 `let checkpointRef = Git.checkpointRef(thread: threadID, turn: turnIndex, phase: "start")`
- ThreadRuntime.swift:2281 `let ref = Git.checkpointRef(thread: threadID, turn: turn.index, phase: "end")`
So a ref is literally `refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/<lowercased-uuid-with-hyphens>/<turnIndex>-start` or `.../<turn.index>-end`.
Persisted fields, Timeline.swift:256-257 inside `struct TurnRecord: Codable, Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable`:
```
var baseCheckpoint: String?
var endCheckpoint: String?
```
There is NO explicit `CodingKeys` enum in Timeline.swift (grep for `enum CodingKeys` returns nothing), so the synthesized JSON keys are literally `"baseCheckpoint"` and `"endCheckpoint"`. Field-by-field decode at Timeline.swift:286-287: `baseCheckpoint = container.value(.baseCheckpoint, default: nil)` / `endCheckpoint = container.value(.endCheckpoint, default: nil)`.
Write sites: ThreadRuntime.swift:1250 `updateTurn(turn.id) { $0.baseCheckpoint = checkpointRef }`, guarded by `if await checkpoint.value` (1249) where the task at 1237-1240 is `guard await git.isRepository() else { return false }; return (try? await git.captureCheckpoint(checkpointRef)) != nil`. ThreadRuntime.swift:2279-2283 + 2303-2304: `var endCheckpoint: String?; if turn.baseCheckpoint != nil { let ref = ...phase: "end"); if (try? await git.captureCheckpoint(ref)) != nil { endCheckpoint = ref } }` then `updateTurn(turnID) { if let endCheckpoint { $0.endCheckpoint = endCheckpoint } ... }`. So an end checkpoint is only ever recorded for a turn that already has a base checkpoint.
Read sites: ThreadRuntime.swift:1770 (`turns[index].baseCheckpoint`, else throw `ProviderError.failed("No file checkpoint is available for this message. You can still keep the file changes.")` at :1771), :1775 (`let end = removed.compactMap(\.endCheckpoint).last`), :1816, :1869, :1970, :1997-1999, :3249 (`treeBeforeCommand()` last resort), :3359; AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:517 (`let base = turns.first?.baseCheckpoint`).
MIGRATION: SOURCE FACT -- there is none. The string `refs/droppy-code` occurs at exactly two places repo-wide, Git.swift:410 (construction) and Git.swift:651 (`let prefix = "refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/\(thread.uuidString.lowercased())/"` in `deleteCheckpoints`). No code reads, rewrites or rewrites-on-load a stored checkpoint ref. A stored ref whose namespace no longer exists simply fails at `git diff`/`git restore` time and surfaces as `"Conversation reverted, but files could not be restored: <error>"` (ThreadRuntime.swift:1875).
resolutions.port_impact: ENGINEERING DECISION forced by the absence of migration: the Windows port MUST keep the ref namespace byte-identical, `refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/<lowercase uuid>/<turn>-<phase>`, and the two phase words `start` and `end` exactly. Renaming it to a Marrow/port namespace silently orphans every checkpoint in every user repository and breaks revert for all already-recorded turns, with no code path to notice. The persisted JSON keys `baseCheckpoint` and `endCheckpoint` are likewise fixed. Git refs are case-sensitive on every platform including Windows, so `.uuidString.lowercased()` must be reproduced, not left as .NET/Node's default uppercase or mixed-case GUID rendering.

resolutions.finding: G2 Exact argument vectors missing for six shipped commands.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, verbatim from source. Every one of these is additionally prefixed by Git.run (Git.swift:43) with `["-c", "core.quotepath=false", "-c", "color.ui=false"]` before the subcommand, and run with cwd = `directory`, environment = LoginEnvironment.current + GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 + GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0.
- Git.swift:290 `fetch()` -> `["fetch", "--quiet", "origin"]`, `timeout: 300`, wrapped in `try Self.check(...)`.
- Git.swift:299-300 `changedPaths(from:to:)` -> `output(["diff", "--name-only", "-z", from, to])` then `.split(separator: "\0").map(String.init)`. NO timeout argument -> 120 s default. (R036/critic both silent on the 120 s here; it is the default.)
- Git.swift:259-260 `treeHash(of ref: String)` -> `output(["rev-parse", "\(ref)^{tree}"])` then `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`. The `^{tree}` peel is part of the single argument string, not a separate token.
- Git.swift:263-264 `commitHash(of ref: String = "HEAD")` -> `output(["rev-parse", "--verify", ref])`, trimmed. The default parameter `= "HEAD"` is real and used: AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:212 `let head = try await git.commitHash()` and :241 `guard try await git.commitHash() == head`.
- Git.swift:268-272 `commitWork(_ tree:parent:message:)` -> `run(["commit-tree", tree, "-p", parent, "-F", "-"], input: Data(message.utf8))`, no `environment:`, no `timeout:` (120 s default), returns `result.trimmedOutput`.
- Git.swift:293-294 `isAncestor(_ commit:of other:)` -> `(try? await run(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, other]))?.succeeded ?? false`. Never throws; a git that cannot run answers false, i.e. 'not an ancestor'.
For completeness, the other shipped vectors this family needs and R036 also under-specified:
- :64 `isRepository` -> `["rev-parse", "--is-inside-work-tree"]`, true iff `trimmedOutput == "true"`.
- :68 `repositoryRoot` -> `["rev-parse", "--show-prefix"]`, then one `deleteLastPathComponent()` per `/`-separated component of the trimmed prefix.
- :77 `hasCommits` -> `["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", "HEAD"]`, succeeded.
- :81 `status` -> `["status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch"]`, parsed on the literal prefixes `"# branch.head "`, `"# branch.upstream "`, `"# branch.ab "`; any non-`#` line increments `changedFiles`.
- :101-102 `branches` -> format literal `"%(HEAD)%09%(refname:short)%09%(upstream:short)"`, command `["for-each-ref", "--sort=-committerdate", "--format=<that>", "refs/heads"]`.
- :114 `switchBranch` -> `["switch", name]`; :118 `createBranch` -> `["switch", "-c", name]`.
- :122-124 `addWorktree` -> `["worktree", "add", "-b", branch, path]` + `[base]` when base != nil (no timeout -> 120 s).
- :128 `removeWorktree` -> `["worktree", "remove", "--force", path]`.
- :132 `remoteURL` -> `["remote", "get-url", "origin"]`.
- :150 `listFiles` -> `["ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"]`.
- :157-158 `workingChanges` -> `["status", "--short"]` and `["diff", "HEAD", "--no-ext-diff"]`.
- :164-165 `commitAll` -> `["add", "-A"]` then `["commit", "-F", "-"]` with the message on stdin.
- :169 `push` -> `["push", "-u", "origin", "HEAD"]`, 300.
- :234 `defaultBranch` -> `["symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"]`, then per candidate in the literal array `["main", "master"]` `["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/remotes/origin/<candidate>"]`, else the literal `"main"`.
- :252-254 `captureTree(paths:)` -> `["read-tree", "HEAD"]` (only when hasCommits), then `["add", "-A", "--ignore-errors", "--pathspec-from-file=-", "--pathspec-file-nul"]` (300 s, NUL-separated paths on stdin), then `["write-tree"]`.
- :275 `updateRef(_:to:)` -> `["update-ref", ref, commit]`. :282 `updateRef(_:to:expecting:)` -> `["update-ref", ref, commit, old ?? ""]` (empty string = must not exist).
- :286 `pushBranch` -> `["push", "-u", "origin", "refs/heads/\(name):refs/heads/\(name)"]`, 300.
- :305 `dirtyPaths` -> `["status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=all"]`.
- :323 `ignoredPaths` -> `["check-ignore", "-z", "--stdin"]`, accepted when `result.succeeded || result.status == 1`.
- :347 `presentPaths` -> `["cat-file", "--batch-check=%(objecttype)", "-Z"]`, stdin is `"<ref>:<path>\0"` per path, an answer counts as present iff `!answer.hasSuffix(" missing")`.
- :373 `hasOperationInProgress` -> `["rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-dir"]`.
- :383 `resetSoft` -> `["reset", "--soft", "--quiet", commit]`.
- :389 `resetIndex` -> `["reset", "--quiet", "--pathspec-from-file=-", "--pathspec-file-nul"]`.
- :395 `checkoutPaths` -> `["checkout", "--quiet", ref, "--"] + paths`.
- :400 `removePaths` -> `["rm", "--quiet", "--"] + paths`.
- :404 `pullFastForward` -> `["pull", "--ff-only", "--quiet"]`, 300.
- :423 `captureCheckpoint` commit -> `["commit-tree", tree, "-m", "Droppy Code checkpoint"]` with `environment: Self.identity`; then :428 `["update-ref", ref, commit]`.
- :448 incremental scratch add -> `["add", "-A", "--pathspec-from-file=-", "--pathspec-file-nul"]`, 300 (note: NO `--ignore-errors`, unlike :253).
- :459/:484/:707 full add -> `["add", "-A", "--", "."]`, 300.
- :529 `indexPath` -> `["rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-path", "index"]`.
- :586 `previewRestore` numstat -> `["diff", "--numstat", "-z", "--no-renames", "--no-ext-diff", base, end, "--"] + paths`.
- :608 `restore` -> `["restore", "--source", ref, "--worktree", "--staged", "--pathspec-from-file=-", "--pathspec-file-nul"]`, stdin = ABSOLUTE paths joined by \0; :616 `["rm", "-q", "--cached", "--ignore-unmatch", "--pathspec-from-file=-", "--pathspec-file-nul"]`, same stdin shape.
- :625 `blobs` -> `["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-name", ref, "--"] + absolute paths`.
- :643 `workingBlobs` -> `["hash-object", "--stdin-paths"]`, stdin = absolute paths joined by \n.
- :652 `deleteCheckpoints` -> `["for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)", prefix]`, then `["update-ref", "--stdin"]` with `"delete <ref>\n"` per ref.
- :669-670 `commitTree` -> `["commit-tree", tree, "-m", message]` + `["-p", "HEAD"]` when hasCommits, `environment: Self.identity`.
- :679 `addDetachedWorktree` -> `["worktree", "add", "--detach", path, commit]`, 300.
- :684 `pruneWorktrees` -> `["worktree", "prune"]`.
- :693 `apply` plain -> `["apply", "--binary", "--whitespace=nowarn", "-"]`; :708 three-way -> `["apply", "--3way", "--binary", "--whitespace=nowarn", "-"]` with GIT_INDEX_FILE set.
resolutions.port_impact: These vectors are the specification. The port builds each argv as an ordered array, never as a joined command string: several arguments contain characters CMD and PowerShell would mangle (`^{tree}`, `refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x`, `%(refname)`, `--batch-check=%(objecttype)`). On Windows the port must pass the argv through a CreateProcess-style spawn with explicit argument escaping (Node `child_process.spawn` with `shell: false`), because `%(...)` is percent-expansion in CMD and `^` is CMD's escape character. Stdin payloads that are NUL-separated must be written as raw bytes, not as a newline-normalized string.

resolutions.finding: G3 diff(from:to:binary:paths:) boundary: chunk guard is `>` not `>=`, and `paths: []` produces a full-tree diff with no early return.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must implement the boundary as `> 400`, not `>= 400`, or it changes how many git processes a 400-file turn spawns. It must NOT add an empty-paths early return: that would be a behaviour change from the source, even though it is latent today. It must keep `--literal-pathspecs` conditional on `paths != nil` (so a nil-paths diff does NOT get it) and placed before the `diff` subcommand. Chunk joining (Git.swift:568) inserts a `\n` only when the accumulated output is non-empty and does not already end in one.

resolutions.finding: G4 R036's unresolved_question 'isBuildOutput has no call site in this bundle' -- critic says seven sites, all silent filters with no user-visible report.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT on the count: exactly SEVEN executable call sites, which I enumerate and count:
1. AppModel+Hydra.swift:251 `paths = paths.filter { path in !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput(path) && projects.contains { TouchedPaths.relative(path, root: $0.path) != nil } }`
2. AppModel+Hydra.swift:754 (inside `hydraWork`) `let paths = changed.filter { !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput($0) }`
3. AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:144 `var leftover = Set(changed.filter { !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput($0) })`
4. AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:503 `for path in reported where !path.isEmpty && !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput(path) {`
5. AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:530 `paths = paths.filter { !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput($0) }`
6. ThreadRuntime.swift:3288 `let real = changed.filter { !$0.isEmpty && !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput($0) && !attributed.contains($0) }`
7. ThreadRuntime.swift:3347 `hydraTouched.formUnion(paths.filter { !$0.isEmpty && !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput($0) })`
(AppModel+Hydra.swift:745 is a doc comment naming the function, not a call.)
CRITIC IS WRONG on 'Nothing surfaces "this file was excluded"'. Site 2 is counted and reported. AppModel+Hydra.swift:752-756:
```
private static func hydraWork(in copyGit: Git, from base: String, to after: String) async throws -> (paths: [String], droppedBuildOutputFiles: Int) {
    let changed = try await copyGit.changedPaths(from: base, to: after)
    let paths = changed.filter { !TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput($0) }
    return (paths, changed.count - paths.count)
}
```
That count flows to AppModel+Hydra.swift:738 `droppedBuildOutputFiles: work.droppedBuildOutputFiles`, to :706 `landing.droppedBuildOutputFiles = prepared.droppedBuildOutputFiles`, is persisted (Hydra.swift:467 `var droppedBuildOutputFiles = 0`, decoded at :481), and becomes USER-VISIBLE text at Hydra.swift:1321:
```
let omitted = landing.droppedBuildOutputFiles == 0 ? "" : "; \(landing.droppedBuildOutputFiles) build-output file\(landing.droppedBuildOutputFiles == 1 ? " was" : "s were") left out"
```
appended to one of three sentences at Hydra.swift:1322-1324: `"Did not land: \(listed)\(omitted)."`, `"Did not land (\(error)): \(listed)\(omitted)."`, `"Landed in your checkout: \(listed)\(omitted)."`. So a user reading a head's landing summary sees e.g. `Landed in your checkout: a.swift (+3 -1); 2,700 build-output files were left out.` (the count is interpolated bare, unformatted). The other six sites ARE silent.
SOURCE FACT on the predicate, TouchedPaths.swift:39-52. `isBuildOutput` splits the path on `/` with `omittingEmptySubsequences: true` and returns true if ANY component `== ".DS_Store"`, OR `hasSuffix(".noindex")`, OR is in `buildOutputNames`. `buildOutputNames` has exactly FIFTEEN elements, counted: `-Xcc`, `DerivedData`, `.build`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `xcuserdata`, `.swiftpm`, `ModuleCache`, `.gradle`, `.turbo`, `.parcel-cache`, `.commandcode`. Matching is exact and CASE-SENSITIVE (Swift `Set<String>.contains`).
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the 15-element set verbatim, exact case, plus the two dynamic rules (`.DS_Store` exact component, `.noindex` suffix). Do NOT case-fold on Windows even though NTFS is case-insensitive: a repository checked out on Windows can legitimately hold `Build/` and the source would not exclude it; folding would silently drop user work. Reproduce the counted-and-reported behaviour at the hydra landing path (one user-visible sentence) and the silence at the other six sites. The plural/singular switch is `" was"` vs `"s were"` appended to `"build-output file"` -- note the leading space in `" was"`.

resolutions.finding: G5 TouchedPaths.matches -- where is it consumed?
resolutions.port_impact: The port must implement `matches` with the bidirectional `/`-anchored suffix rule exactly, including the `oldPath` arm, because it is load-bearing for both (a) which rows auto-expand and where the panel scrolls, and (b) de-duplicating synthesized per-edit diff cards against the parsed patch. On Windows the port must normalize agent-reported paths to forward slashes BEFORE calling it, since the rule is literally `"/" + path` and a backslash-separated path would never match.

resolutions.finding: G6 previewRestore path-space question: are `paths` and the blob lookups in the same space?
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, and the answer is subtler than the critic states. The caller: ThreadRuntime.swift:1768-1777:
```
guard let app, let thread, let project = app.project(thread.projectID),
      let index = turns.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == turnID }), let base = turns[index].baseCheckpoint else {
    throw ProviderError.failed("No file checkpoint is available for this message. You can still keep the file changes.")
}
let removed = turns[index...]
let paths = Set(removed.flatMap { $0.touchedPaths ?? [] }).sorted()
let end = removed.compactMap(\.endCheckpoint).last
return try await Git(thread.worktreePath ?? project.path).previewRestore(base: base, end: end, paths: paths)
```
`touchedPaths` are produced at ThreadRuntime.swift:2277 + 2288-2291 with `let root = thread.worktreePath ?? project.path` and `TouchedPaths.relative(edit.path, root: root)` -- i.e. relative to the PROJECT/WORKTREE directory, the same directory `Git(...)` is bound to. So `paths` are cwd-relative, NOT necessarily repository-root-relative.
Inside previewRestore (Git.swift:581-597):
- :584 `if let known { end = known } else { end = try await captureTree(paths: paths) }` -- the fallback feeds `paths` to `add --pathspec-from-file=-` with cwd = `directory`, so they are read as cwd-relative. Correct.
- :586 `RevertPreview(numstat: await output(["diff", "--numstat", "-z", "--no-renames", "--no-ext-diff", base, end, "--"] + paths))` -- the pathspecs are again cwd-relative. Correct. BUT git's `diff` output paths are repository-root-relative by default (it is `--relative`/`diff.relative` that would make them cwd-relative, and Git.run sets neither; Git.run's only `-c` options are `core.quotepath=false` and `color.ui=false`, Git.swift:43). So `preview.files[].path` comes back in REPO-ROOT space, a different space from the `paths` that went in.
- :588-590 `let root = try await repositoryRoot()`, then `blobs(in: end, at: preview.files.map(\.path), root: root)` and `workingBlobs(at: preview.files.map(\.path), root: root)` -- both join `preview.files[].path` (repo-root space) onto the repository root. CONSISTENT.
- `blobs` keys its result by `ls-tree --full-name` output, which is repo-root-relative. CONSISTENT with `file.path`.
- The consumer, ThreadRuntime.swift:1873 `try await Git(directory).restore(preview.restorable.map(\.path), from: base)`, and `restore` (Git.swift:601-621) again does `let root = try await repositoryRoot()` and builds ABSOLUTE paths from it (:609, :617, :619). CONSISTENT.
SO: the pipeline is internally consistent AFTER the numstat step, because the numstat step itself re-bases from cwd space into repo-root space. The critic's conclusion -- that the two spaces coincide only when the project path IS the repository root -- is right about the INPUT side (`paths` as pathspecs, and `captureTree(paths:)`) but wrong to imply the blob lookups are mis-keyed. Nothing guards the subdirectory case, and nothing in the code detects it.
SOURCE FACT, fragility: the whole scheme silently depends on git's DEFAULT of non-relative diff output. A user with `diff.relative = true` in their git config would make :586 return cwd-relative paths while :588-590 still join them onto the repository root, producing wrong absolute paths and therefore `isKept` decided on a missing file. Git.run does not neutralize `diff.relative`.
Also SOURCE FACT: `previewRestore` has an early return, `guard !paths.isEmpty else { return RevertPreview(files: []) }` (Git.swift:582), and `restore` has `guard !paths.isEmpty else { return }` (Git.swift:602).
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the mixed spaces exactly -- cwd-relative pathspecs in, repo-root-relative paths out, repository-root-joined absolutes for the blob lookups. Do NOT 'fix' it by normalizing everything to one space: that would change which files are marked `isKept` in the project-is-a-subdirectory case. Do NOT add `-c diff.relative=false`; the source does not. On Windows this path is the highest-risk one in the family because `URL.appendingPathComponent`'s macOS semantics become `path.join`/`path.resolve` semantics, and because the stdin payloads at Git.swift:609/617 are absolute paths joined by \0, which on Windows carry drive letters and backslashes -- git for Windows accepts them but they must not be forward-slash-normalized selectively, since the numstat-derived `file.path` halves stay forward-slashed.

resolutions.finding: G7 R036's unresolved_question on forge cases.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce three cases, no fourth. Reproduce the asymmetric parsing exactly (search for `merge_requests` at index >= 1; fixed `parts[2]` for `pull`/`pulls`), and `number > 0`. Reproduce `!N` for GitLab and `#N` everywhere else, since it appears in popover chrome and in chat notes. Reproduce `forge()`'s lowercased substring test with `.gitea` as the fallthrough: an enterprise GitHub at `git.acme.com` will be driven with `tea`, which is upstream behaviour, not a bug to fix.

resolutions.finding: G8 WorkingTreeWatch teardown asymmetry: the cookie-timeout path calls the same tearDown() the registry path's comment warns about.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT to reproduce, not fix: the port's watch equivalent must delete the shared scratch index on cookie timeout, unguarded by any in-flight capture check, and must reproduce the once-only guard (a second teardown is a no-op because the stream handle is already nil). The user-visible consequence to preserve is that the affected turn silently gets no checkpoint and its revert later throws `"No file checkpoint is available for this message. You can still keep the file changes."` (ThreadRuntime.swift:1771). On Windows the FSEvents layer becomes ReadDirectoryChangesW; the cookie mechanism (write a file, wait for its own event, 1 s ceiling) transfers directly, and the same race must be preserved.

resolutions.finding: G9 A watch torn down by the cookie timeout stays in the registry forever; the directory never gets a live watch again.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT, and the stickiness is exactly as described. `state.stream` is assigned in exactly two places: `init` (WorkingTreeWatch.swift:150 `state.withLock { $0.stream = handle }`, only when `FSEventStreamStart` returns true) and `tearDown` (:161 `defer { state.stream = nil }`). There is no restart path -- no `FSEventStreamStart` outside init (grep-verifiable: the only occurrence is :148).
After a cookie-timeout tearDown: `settledGeneration()` short-circuits at :247 `guard state.withLock({ $0.stream }) != nil else { return nil }`; `currentTree` :296 takes `return try await capture(nil, nil)`; Git's closure (Git.swift:436) takes `guard let scratch else { return try await captureTree() }` -- a fresh UUID index, seeded, full `add -A -- .`, deleted. Every snapshot for that directory, forever.
Removal from the registry: `watches` (:86, `Mutex<[(directory: String, watch: WorkingTreeWatch)]>([])`) is mutated in exactly one function, `shared` (:101-105): `watches.append(...)` and `watches.count > limit ? watches.removeFirst().watch : nil` with `limit = 32` (:87). `removeFirst()` evicts the OLDEST entry, which is not in general the dead one. And `shared`'s first statement (:93) `if let existing = watches.withLock({ $0.first { $0.directory == directory }?.watch }) { return existing }` hands the dead watch straight back to every later caller. So the directory is stuck on the slow path until 32 OTHER directories have been registered after it and FIFO eviction happens to reach it, or the app restarts.
Second-order: that eventual FIFO eviction calls `dropped.tearDown()` (:106), which for the already-dead watch returns immediately at :163 (stream already nil) and so does NOT re-delete the scratch -- but it also means the dead watch's scratch file, deleted once at timeout, is simply gone and the object is released.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the stickiness: one cookie timeout permanently demotes that directory to full-capture-per-snapshot for the process lifetime (modulo 32-entry FIFO eviction). Do NOT add a restart or a health check. This matters more on Windows than on macOS: a directory on a network share, a mapped drive, or a VM-shared folder is far likelier to miss the cookie event, so Windows users will hit the demoted path more often -- which is correct parity, and is the reason the source demotes rather than trusting a flaky watcher. The port must also reproduce the pre-check at :94 `guard (try? URL(fileURLWithPath: directory).resourceValues(forKeys: [.volumeIsLocalKey]))?.volumeIsLocal == true else { return nil }` -- on Windows the equivalent is GetDriveType, and a non-local volume must yield NO watch at all, i.e. the fresh-capture path from the very first snapshot.

resolutions.finding: G10 Git.run merges the caller's `extra` LAST, so a caller could override GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Git.swift:36-48:
```
) async throws -> ShellResult {
    var environment = LoginEnvironment.current
    environment["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
    environment["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
    environment.merge(extra) { _, new in new }
    return try await Shell.run(
        Self.executable,
        ["-c", "core.quotepath=false", "-c", "color.ui=false"] + arguments,
        in: directory,
        environment: environment,
        input: input,
        timeout: timeout
    )
}
```
`merge(extra) { _, new in new }` takes the caller's value on every collision, so `extra` has the LAST word over both variables and over everything in LoginEnvironment.current.
SOURCE FACT on shipped callers: `extra` is non-empty at exactly six sites in Git.swift, and every one passes only one of two things:
- `["GIT_INDEX_FILE": index.path]` at :251 (captureTree(paths:)), :446 (captureTree(scratch:paths:)), :476 (captureTree()), :701 (apply's three-way index).
- `Self.identity` at :423 (captureCheckpoint's commit-tree) and :671 (commitTree). `Self.identity` (Git.swift:660-663) is exactly four keys: `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "Droppy Code"`, `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "droppy-code@localhost"`, `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: "Droppy Code"`, `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: "droppy-code@localhost"`.
Neither key collides with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT or GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS, so no shipped call overrides them. R036's claim that the two variables are 'always set on git' is true for the shipped code and false as a general statement about the function.
resolutions.port_impact: Implement the precedence in this exact order -- base environment, then the two forced variables, then the caller's extras last -- rather than the intuitive 'forced variables win'. It is latent today but it is the function's contract, and a port that hardens it would diverge the first time a new caller is added. Note also that GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 is what keeps the app's status/diff calls from taking the index.lock; on Windows, where file locking is mandatory rather than advisory, dropping it would make the app's background snapshots collide with the user's own git in a terminal.

resolutions.finding: G11 DiffParser: the `--- ` branch consumes every `--- ` line and only `--- /dev/null` has an effect; oldPath never comes from `---`.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must implement the `--- ` arm as a consuming branch whose only effect is the exact-string test against `"--- /dev/null"`, and must NOT derive oldPath from it. Deriving oldPath from `--- a/foo` would populate `DiffFile.oldPath` on every modified file, which then feeds `TouchedPaths.matches` (which tests `[file.path, file.oldPath]`) and would widen every focus/de-dup match in DiffInspector. Note also that `-M` is passed on the app's own diffs (Git.swift:553), so rename headers do occur, while previewRestore's numstat passes `--no-renames` (Git.swift:586).

resolutions.finding: G12 RevertPreview: the outer numstat split omits empty subsequences, the inner one does not.
resolutions.port_impact: Split records on NUL discarding empties; split each record on TAB with at most 2 splits and KEEPING empties. Empty numstat text must yield an empty file list and no error. On Windows, git for Windows emits the same `-z` framing; the port must read the stdout as bytes and decode UTF-8 without any CRLF translation, since `-z` output carries no newlines and a text-mode pipe would be harmless but a `\r\n` normalization of a path containing `\r` would not.

resolutions.finding: CC1 Two git identities: commitWork runs WITHOUT Self.identity, so a head's branch commit carries the user's own git config identity.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Git.swift:660-663:
```
private static let identity = [
    "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "Droppy Code", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "droppy-code@localhost",
    "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "Droppy Code", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "droppy-code@localhost",
]
```
Four keys, two distinct values, verbatim: `"Droppy Code"` and `"droppy-code@localhost"`.
Three commit-creating call sites, counted:
1. Git.swift:423 `captureCheckpoint` -> `run(["commit-tree", tree, "-m", "Droppy Code checkpoint"], environment: Self.identity)` -- Droppy Code identity.
2. Git.swift:669-671 `commitTree(_ tree:message:)` -> `var arguments = ["commit-tree", tree, "-m", message]; if await hasCommits() { arguments += ["-p", "HEAD"] }; let result = try await run(arguments, environment: Self.identity)` -- Droppy Code identity. Its one call site is AppModel+Hydra.swift:52, `let commit = try await git.commitTree(tree, message: "Droppy Code: a Hydra head's starting point")`.
3. Git.swift:268-272 `commitWork(_ tree:parent:message:)` -> `run(["commit-tree", tree, "-p", parent, "-F", "-"], input: Data(message.utf8))` -- NO `environment:` argument. `extra` therefore defaults to `[:]`, nothing overrides, and git falls back to the checkout's own `user.name`/`user.email`.
`commitWork` has exactly one call site: AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:235 `let commit = try await git.commitWork(tree, parent: head, message: message)`. That commit is then written to a branch (`git.updateRef("refs/heads/\(branch)", to: commit, expecting: ownBranch ? nil : head)`, :248) and PUSHED to origin (`try await git.pushBranch(branch)`, :255), and a merge/pull request is opened for it (:261). So the only commit that leaves the machine is the one in the user's own name; the two internal-only commits (a checkpoint, and a worktree's detached starting point) are the ones stamped Droppy Code.
resolutions.port_impact: This split is deliberate and must be copied exactly. The port must NOT pass an identity on the commit-work path -- a Marrow-branded author on a pushed commit would show up in the user's repository history and on the forge. Conversely it must pass the Droppy Code identity on the two internal commits, so that a user with no `user.email` configured can still be checkpointed (git refuses commit-tree without an identity). ENGINEERING DECISION for the port: keep the literals `"Droppy Code"` and `"droppy-code@localhost"` if byte-parity of the object graph matters (checkpoint commit hashes are not compared anywhere, so it does not), but note that changing them changes nothing user-visible because these commits are parentless and ref-only (see CC2). The commit-tree message literal `"Droppy Code checkpoint"` is likewise internal-only.

resolutions.finding: CC2 Checkpoint commits are PARENTLESS.
resolutions.port_impact: The port MUST NOT add `-p HEAD` to the checkpoint commit. Doing so would (a) pin the whole history under a hidden ref so gc could never reclaim a deleted thread's checkpoints, and (b) make the checkpoint commits reachable in `--all` traversals, changing `git log --all`, `git fsck`, and repack behaviour in the user's repository. Reproduce the ref-deletion path verbatim, including that its failure is swallowed (`_ = try? await run(...)`), so a delete that fails leaves the refs and is never reported.

resolutions.finding: CC3 Forge CLIs run in a different environment from git -- no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. The six forge-CLI invocations are Git.swift:181, 186, 191 (createPullRequest) and 216, 217, 218 (mergePullRequest). Every one has the shape `try await Shell.run(tool: "<glab|gh|tea>", <args>, in: directory, timeout: 300)` -- no `environment:` argument.
`Shell.run(tool:)` (Shell.swift:121-133) declares `environment: [String: String]? = nil` and forwards it unchanged: `return try await run(executable, arguments, in: directory, environment: environment, input: input, timeout: timeout)`. The primitive `Shell.run` then does, at Shell.swift:49, `process.environment = environment ?? LoginEnvironment.current`. So the forge CLIs get LoginEnvironment.current RAW -- neither of the two variables Git.run forces at Git.swift:38-39.
The exact argv of all six, verbatim and in order:
- glab create: `["mr", "create", "--title", title, "--description", body, "--yes"]` + `["--source-branch", source]` if source + `["--target-branch", target]` if target.
- gh create: `["pr", "create", "--title", title, "--body", body]` + `["--head", source]` + `["--base", target]`.
- tea create: `["pulls", "create", "--title", title, "--description", body]` + `["--head", source]` + `["--base", target]`.
- glab merge: `["mr", "merge", number, "--yes"]`.
- gh merge: `["pr", "merge", number, "--merge"]`.
- tea merge: `["pulls", "merge", number]`.
Note `--yes` on both glab commands and `--body` vs `--description` differing between gh and the other two.
The URL is scraped out of the combined streams: Git.swift:194-196 `let text = result.output + "\n" + result.errorOutput; let match = text.firstMatch(of: #/https:\/\/\S+/#); return match.flatMap { URL(string: String($0.output)) }` -- the regex literal is `https://\S+`, first match wins, and the function returns `URL?` so a CLI that prints no https URL yields nil rather than an error.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must NOT hoist GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 into a shared spawn helper. gh/glab/tea keep their own credentials and their own prompting behaviour, and the source deliberately lets them prompt; forcing the git variables onto them would change how an unauthenticated gh behaves. The practical Windows consequence to preserve: an unauthenticated forge CLI can block until the 300 s timeout, at which point the port's terminate-and-kill path yields a failure whose message is the CLI's own stderr. Reproduce the argv exactly, including `--description` for glab and tea versus `--body` for gh, and the `https://\S+` first-match URL scrape over stdout + "\n" + stderr.

resolutions.finding: CC4 Missing forge CLI throws an exact string R036 left unresolved.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Shell.swift:129-131:
```
guard let executable = LoginEnvironment.which(name) else {
    throw ShellError("\(name) was not found on your PATH.")
}
```
With `name` being literally `"glab"`, `"gh"` or `"tea"`, the user sees exactly one of: `glab was not found on your PATH.`, `gh was not found on your PATH.`, `tea was not found on your PATH.` -- note the trailing period and the capital-free `on your PATH`. `ShellError` (Shell.swift:22-28) is a `LocalizedError` whose `errorDescription` is the message, so `error.localizedDescription` returns it unchanged.
This throw happens BEFORE any process is spawned and is NOT caught inside Git.swift: `createPullRequest` (:174-197) has no do/catch and `mergePullRequest`'s `for` body does `let result: ShellResult ... = try await Shell.run(tool:...)` with the `try` propagating straight out of the function, so a missing CLI aborts on the FIRST iteration without ever reaching the retry logic or `lastFailure`.
Where it surfaces: AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:277-278 wraps the merge in a catch that renders `\(error.localizedDescription)` into both a `HydraMergeRecord` detail and a chat note.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the literal exactly: `<name> was not found on your PATH.` On Windows, PATH lookup is not `which`: the port must resolve against PATHEXT (`gh.exe`, `gh.cmd`, `gh.bat`) as well as the bare name, and must split PATH on `;` not `:` (see CC5). The error message must still say `PATH` in caps with that exact wording, because it is the string the user reads. Also preserve that a missing CLI short-circuits mergePullRequest before the first attempt, so no retry delay is incurred.

resolutions.finding: CC5 macOS-only git resolution -- LoginEnvironment.git, developerGit, which's ':' PATH split.
resolutions.port_impact:
Every line here is a Windows decision, and the port must make each one explicitly rather than transliterate:
1. `which` splits on `:` -- Windows PATH splits on `;`, and Windows has no execute bit, so the executability test becomes a PATHEXT-aware existence test.
2. `name.contains("/")` as the 'this is a path, not a name' test must also accept `\` and a `C:` drive prefix.
3. The whole `developerGit` / xcode-select branch is macOS-only and has NO Windows analogue. The port resolves git from PATH, then from the well-known install locations (`%ProgramFiles%\Git\cmd\git.exe`, `%ProgramFiles%\Git\bin\git.exe`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Git\cmd\git.exe`), then fails with a message. It must NOT hard-code `/usr/bin/git` as a last resort.
4. The login-shell capture (`$SHELL -l -i -c "printf ...; /usr/bin/env -0; ..."`) has no Windows equivalent; the port reads the process environment plus the user/machine registry Environment keys. The PATH augmentation list must be replaced wholesale -- `/opt/homebrew/bin` etc. are meaningless -- with the Windows equivalents for the same tools.
5. `LANG = "en_US.UTF-8"` when absent: keep, because git for Windows honours it for message encoding.
6. Keep the single-shot memoization and the pre-load fallback shape: callers that resolve git before the environment read finishes must still get an answer.

resolutions.finding: CC6 Git.run never passes outputLimit, so every git invocation buffers stdout/stderr unbounded.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. `Shell.run` declares `outputLimit: Int? = nil` (Shell.swift:43) and hands it to `OutputCollector(limit: outputLimit)` (:58). `OutputCollector.append` (:280-284) is `buffer.append(data); guard let limit, buffer.count > limit * 2 else { return }; buffer = Data(buffer.suffix(limit))` -- with nil there is no trimming at all.
Git.run (Git.swift:41-48) passes `Self.executable, arguments, in:, environment:, input:, timeout:` and NOTHING else; `outputLimit` is omitted, so it is nil for every git invocation in the app.
Counted repo-wide, `outputLimit` is passed at exactly TWO call sites, both outside this family: OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:1144 (`timeout: 30, outputLimit: 64_000`) and OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:1159 (`timeout: 120, outputLimit: 24_000`). (Timeline.swift:137 `static let outputLimit = 60_000` is an unrelated constant used at Timeline.swift:165-166 to trim a stored tool output to `"…" + String(output.suffix(30_000))`.)
R036's 40,000 note is a different thing entirely: Git.swift:159 `if patch.utf8.count > 40_000 { patch = String(patch.prefix(40_000)) }` inside `workingChanges()`, applied to an already fully-buffered string.
So the largest unbounded reads in this family are `diff(binary: true)` (Git.swift:547-573, used at AppModel+Hydra.swift:727 and :937 with `binary: true`, which inlines whole binary blobs base85-encoded) and `apply`'s stderr. A head that added a 200 MB asset produces a patch read entirely into memory and then handed to `DiffParser.parse` and written to a `.patch` file (AppModel+Hydra.swift:939-940).
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the unbounded capture for git. Do NOT add a cap: the app relies on getting the complete patch (it writes it to disk at AppModel+Hydra.swift:940 and applies it with `git apply`), and a truncated binary patch would not apply. The port must therefore size its buffers for this and expect multi-hundred-megabyte strings on the hydra landing path. Also reproduce the `workingChanges` trim exactly as written -- see the upstream defect note about `utf8.count` vs `prefix` counting characters.

upstream_defects: Git.swift:159 -- `workingChanges()` tests bytes but trims characters: `if patch.utf8.count > 40_000 { patch = String(patch.prefix(40_000)) }`. `String.prefix(_:)` counts Characters (grapheme clusters), so for a patch of non-ASCII source the kept text can be several times 40,000 bytes (up to ~160 KB for 4-byte scalars, more for multi-scalar graphemes). The port must copy the mismatch: test UTF-8 byte count, then take a 40,000-GRAPHEME prefix. Using a byte-prefix would both change the payload size sent to the model and risk splitting a code point.

Git.swift:213-225 -- `mergePullRequest` burns a final, pointless retry delay. On the last iteration (`attempt == 5`) a GitLab failure that matches the retry predicate still executes `try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3 + attempt * 2))` = 13 seconds, and then the `for` loop simply ends and line 226 throws. A full GitLab retry sequence sleeps 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 = 48 seconds before reporting failure, of which the last 13 are wasted. Reproduce, do not restructure the loop.

Git.swift:223 -- the retry predicate is a lowercased substring test over stdout+stderr: `text.contains("405") || text.contains("not allowed") || text.contains("checking")`. `"405"` matches any output containing those three digits anywhere, including inside a request number, a line number, a byte count or a commit hash prefix. Reproduce the substring test verbatim.

Git.swift:625 (`blobs`), :607-609 and :616-617 (`restore`), :395 (`checkoutPaths`), :400 (`removePaths`) -- these pass user file paths to git as PATHSPECS without `--literal-pathspecs`, while `diff` (Git.swift:552) is careful to add it whenever paths are given. A repository file whose name contains `*`, `?`, `[` or a leading `:` is therefore treated as a glob or a pathspec magic prefix on the restore/checkout/remove/ls-tree paths but as a literal on the diff path. The port must reproduce the inconsistency: adding `--literal-pathspecs` to the restore path would change which files a revert touches.

Git.swift:253 vs :448 -- the two `--pathspec-from-file` adds differ: `captureTree(paths:)` passes `--ignore-errors`, the incremental scratch add does not. So a path that git cannot read takes down the scratch capture (falling through to the delete-and-reseed at :453-459) but is merely skipped in `captureTree(paths:)`. Reproduce both flag sets exactly.

Git.swift:347-353 -- `presentPaths` pairs answers to paths with `zip(paths, answers)`, which silently truncates to the shorter sequence. If `git cat-file --batch-check` emits fewer records than paths (a crash mid-stream, a timeout kill at 120 s), the unanswered tail is silently reported as ABSENT rather than as an error, and `trackedPaths` then excludes those files from a hydra merge. Contrast Git.swift:645-646, where `workingBlobs` DOES check the count and throws `ShellError("git hash-object answered for \(hashes.count) of \(existing.count) files.")`. The asymmetry is upstream; reproduce it.

WorkingTreeWatch.swift:271 vs :96-100 -- the cookie-timeout `tearDown()` deletes the shared scratch index while another caller's detached capture may be writing through it, which is the exact hazard the registry-eviction path documents and avoids. The observable effect is a lost checkpoint for that turn and, later, the revert error `"No file checkpoint is available for this message. You can still keep the file changes."` (ThreadRuntime.swift:1771). See resolution G8.

WorkingTreeWatch.swift:159-170 + :92-108 -- a watch torn down by a cookie timeout is never rebuilt and is handed back to every later caller by `shared`'s fast path at :93, so that directory is permanently demoted to a full fresh capture per snapshot until FIFO eviction at `limit = 32` happens to reach it. See resolution G9.

Git.swift:547-573 -- `diff(paths: [])` (non-nil, empty) emits `--literal-pathspecs ... <from> <to> --` and produces a FULL-TREE diff instead of an empty one, with no early return of the kind every neighbouring path-taking method has. Unreachable today because all three `paths:` call sites guard on non-emptiness (AppModel+Hydra.swift:726, :936; ThreadRuntime.swift:3289). Reproduce the missing guard.

Git.swift:586-590 -- `previewRestore` feeds cwd-relative pathspecs to `git diff --numstat` but consumes the repo-root-relative paths it returns, joining them onto `repositoryRoot()`. Self-consistent only because git's default diff output is repo-root-relative; a user with `diff.relative = true` in their git config breaks it, and Git.run does not neutralize the setting (its only `-c` options are `core.quotepath=false` and `color.ui=false`, Git.swift:43). See resolution G6.

Git.swift:650-656 -- `deleteCheckpoints` discards its own result: `_ = try? await run(["update-ref", "--stdin"], input: ...)`. A failed batch delete leaves the refs, and therefore the checkpoint commits, in the user's repository with nothing reported anywhere. Reproduce the silence.

Git.swift:67-74 -- `repositoryRoot()` derives the root by calling `deleteLastPathComponent()` once per `/`-separated component of `rev-parse --show-prefix`, starting from the Git instance's own `directory` URL. It never asks git for the root directly (`--show-toplevel` exists). Any discrepancy between the URL Foundation built and the path git resolved -- a symlinked project directory, a case-differing path, a trailing component git normalized -- yields a wrong root, and that root is what `blobs`, `workingBlobs` and `restore` join every path onto. On Windows this is the most likely place for a path-normalization divergence (8.3 short names, drive-letter case, junctions). Reproduce the component-counting algorithm rather than substituting `--show-toplevel`.
dead_or_unreachable: Git.swift:274-276, the two-argument overload `func updateRef(_ ref: String, to commit: String) async throws { try Self.check(await run(["update-ref", ref, commit])) }` is DEAD. Proof: a repo-wide grep for `updateRef` over every .swift file returns exactly three hits -- the two declarations (Git.swift:274, :281) and ONE call, AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:248 `try await git.updateRef("refs/heads/\(branch)", to: commit, expecting: ownBranch ? nil : head)`, which resolves to the THREE-argument overload at :281. The one place inside Git.swift that would naturally use the two-arg helper, `captureCheckpoint` at Git.swift:428, instead calls the primitive directly: `try Self.check(await run(["update-ref", ref, commit]))`. There is no test target in this checkout (DroppyCode contains only App, Core, Resources, Services, UI). The Windows port may omit this overload, or keep it for shape parity; nothing observes it.

Git.swift:212, the string literal `"The request could not be merged."` is UNREACHABLE. Proof: it is the initial value of `var lastFailure`; the only read is `throw ShellError(lastFailure)` at :226; the only route to :226 is out of the bottom of `for attempt in 0..<6` (a non-empty half-open range, so the body runs at least once) or the `break` at :223, and BOTH require having executed :221 `lastFailure = result.failureMessage` in that iteration, because :220 `if result.succeeded { return }` is the only other exit from an iteration. `ShellResult.failureMessage` (Shell.swift:15-19) is provably non-empty: it falls back to `"The command failed with exit code \(status)."`. A repo-wide grep for `could not be merged` returns this single line. It must NOT appear in the port's user-visible string inventory.

Git.swift:552, the `paths == nil ? [] : ["--literal-pathspecs"]` / empty-array combination reaching a bare trailing `--` is UNREACHABLE IN THIS CHECKOUT. Proof: `diff(from:to:binary:paths:)` has exactly five call sites; three pass `paths:` (AppModel+Hydra.swift:727, AppModel+Hydra.swift:937, ThreadRuntime.swift:3289) and each is immediately preceded, in the same `guard` chain or the line before, by a non-emptiness check (`guard !work.paths.isEmpty else { return nil }` at :726; `!work.paths.isEmpty` inside the guard chain at :936; `guard !real.isEmpty` at :3289). The other two (AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:220, ThreadRuntime.swift:2004) pass nil. So `paths: []` never occurs. It is latent, not removed -- the port must keep the code path.

Shell.swift:400-409 `developerGit` and its `/usr/bin/xcode-select -p` probe are LIVE on macOS but have NO Windows analogue: the guard `onPath.path == "/usr/bin/git"` can never be true on Windows, so on the port the entire body is unreachable by construction and the function degenerates to `which("git") ?? <fallback>`. Recorded here so the port does not transliterate an 8-second subprocess probe that can never succeed.

NOT DEAD, contrary to R036's unresolved_question: `TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput` has seven live call sites (AppModel+Hydra.swift:251, :754; AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:144, :503, :530; ThreadRuntime.swift:3288, :3347), and `TouchedPaths.matches` has three (DiffInspector.swift:144, :167, :168). Every public method on `Git` has at least one call site outside Git.swift except the two-arg `updateRef` above; I checked all 41 by grep.
still_unresolved: Whether `git diff --numstat -z` emits repository-root-relative paths in EVERY git version the app supports, which is the unstated assumption holding previewRestore's two path spaces together (resolution G6). Settling this needs the pinned source's minimum-git-version policy, which is not stated anywhere in the checkout I read, plus a behavioural check against a real git; neither is available from source alone. The port should treat the repo-root-relative assumption as the specification and record it as a Windows verification item.

The exact FSEvents-to-ReadDirectoryChangesW mapping for WorkingTreeWatch's `kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents` + `kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer` + the three loss flags (`kFSEventStreamEventFlagMustScanSubDirs | kFSEventStreamEventFlagKernelDropped | kFSEventStreamEventFlagUserDropped`, WorkingTreeWatch.swift:180). The source's contract is legible -- any loss flag sets `everything = true` and nils `state.changed` (:211-212) -- but which Windows notification corresponds to 'the kernel dropped events' (ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR on buffer overflow is the candidate) is a port engineering decision I cannot settle from this source.

Whether the `roots` choice at WorkingTreeWatch.swift:143 -- `let roots = gitRoot.hasPrefix(root + "/") ? [root] : [root, gitRoot]` -- is correct for a linked worktree whose git directory sits at a path that merely SHARES a prefix with the root without being under it (e.g. root `/a/b` and gitRoot `/a/bc/.git`). `hasPrefix(root + "/")` handles that correctly, but I could not find a shipped configuration that produces the two-root case to confirm the intended behaviour; `Git.watch()` (Git.swift:465-468) derives gitDirectory as `(indexPath as NSString).deletingLastPathComponent`, and `indexPath` for a worktree comes from `rev-parse --git-path index` (:529), which for a linked worktree is `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>/index`. The two-root branch is therefore the normal worktree case, but I did not trace a concrete worktree creation end-to-end to confirm the resulting prefix relationship.
